brief:
Israeli election rhetoric centered on security and attacks against Arab political parties has not delivered the decisive outcomes candidates promised, Al Jazeera English reported. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and far-right candidate Itamar Ben-Gvir made aggressive campaign boasts and targeted Arab parties in their messaging ahead of the vote.

The election has produced a deadlocked result, leaving major campaign pledges unfulfilled. The outcome reflects a fragmented political landscape that resists the clear mandates candidates sought through their rhetoric.
dek: From Netanyahu to Ben-Gvir, campaign boasts and attacks on Arab parties have been met with a deadlocked result.
title: Israeli candidates' campaign promises fail to break electoral deadlock
